title: Per-consumer pseudonymity and consumer attestation are not wired into SVID issuance
description:
EXPLOITABLE NOW (privacy/linkability), and it is the exact failure SPEC-HIA calls out as security-critical.

persona-grpc/src/service.rs:175 issues the credential with the raw root identity:
    let spiffe_id_str = claim.spiffe_id.uri();
That string goes into sub, spiffe_id and the response (service.rs:198-204) verbatim, identically for every caller and every audience.

The pseudonymity machinery exists but has ZERO production callers:
  - persona_core::derive_pseudonym (persona-core/src/pseudonym.rs:13) - only referenced by the pub use in persona-core/src/lib.rs:16 and by its own unit tests.
  - SpiffeId::pseudonymous (persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:106) - never called.
  - ConsumerIdentity::selector_key (persona-core/src/consumer.rs:47), documented as "a stable string key suitable for use as HKDF info" - never called.
  - persona_grpc::consumer_attest::attest_peer (persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:16) - never called. persona-grpc/src/server.rs:37-41 hands the raw UnixListenerStream to tonic without attesting any peer, and service.rs:187-196 logs consumer_uid = "unknown".

SPEC-HIA:75 - "The default SPIFFE ID exposed to a consumer is **not** the root identity."
SPEC-HIA:78  - spiffe://{trust-domain}/pseudonym/{hkdf-derived-opaque-id}/for/{consumer-app-id}
SPEC-HIA:193 - "On each FetchJWTSVID or FetchX509SVID call, personad attests the calling process and derives the pseudonym for that consumer."
SPEC-HIA:191 - "**This is the security-critical decision.** If any process in the user session can call the socket without identification, then malware can enumerate the user identities."

CONSEQUENCE: (a) every consumer receives the same global identifier, so any two relying parties that collude link the user across audiences - the headline unlinkability property of the design is absent, not weakened; (b) no consumer is identified at all, so the daemon cannot distinguish a users password manager from malware running as the same uid, and cannot ever scope or revoke per consumer. The 0600 socket mode (server.rs:32) limits callers to the same uid, which is precisely the boundary SPEC-HIA:191 says is insufficient.

This is a wiring gap, not a design gap: the primitive is correct (see the pseudonym.rs vectors, independently confirmed against pyca cryptography HKDF) and just needs attest_peer -> selector_key -> derive_pseudonym -> SpiffeId::pseudonymous plumbed into fetch_jwtsvid. Filing so the shipped-behaviour/spec divergence is tracked rather than implied by dead code.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.41 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
